Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing this letter at the request of Patty Chavez, who has provided me with her medical records. I am Dr. Tina Cooper, a gastroenterologist practicing at the Gray-Alexander Clinic. Patty was seen today for a follow-up regarding her Hepatitis C, a condition she has been managing under my care. Her blood pressure was recorded at 129/76, and her weight was 149 pounds.

Patty has been diagnosed with Hepatitis C since May 22, 2025. At her current visit, we reviewed her condition and noted it remains controlled. There have been no complications such as cirrhosis or sustained virologic response (SVR) observed thus far. Her current treatment regimen, which she has been compliant with, has been effective in managing her Hepatitis C. During today’s Patty did not report any new symptoms or concerns related to her condition.

Previously, on June 2, 2024, Patty was seen for a follow-up on her Hepatitis C. At that time, her blood pressure was 127/75, and her weight was 150 pounds. Her Hepatitis C was noted to be stable and well-controlled. Again, there were no signs of cirrhosis or SVR, and her ongoing treatment plan was reviewed and adjusted as needed.

On April 9, 2023, Patty was seen for her Hepatitis C. At that visit, her blood pressure was 142/73, and her weight was 149 pounds. The diagnosis of Hepatitis C was confirmed, and initial steps were taken to manage her condition effectively. The patient was educated about her condition, and a treatment plan was formulated. Since then, she has been under consistent follow-up, and her condition has remained stable.

In addition to her medical history, Patty’s social history is noteworthy. She is a former smoker who used to smoke 10 cigarettes per day, starting on February 10, 2011. She quit smoking on March 16, 2012. Currently, Patty consumes approximately 12 alcoholic drinks per week. 

Her family history also includes her father, who was diagnosed with myocardial infarction (MI) at the age of 79. He is still alive and well at the age of 84.

Patty has been compliant with her treatment plan and all recommended follow-up appointments. Her Hepatitis C has been well-managed, and she has not experienced any significant complications related to her condition. She continues to receive regular care and monitoring to ensure her condition remains controlled.

I hope this information is helpful. If have any further questions or require additional details, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Sincerely,

Dr. Tina Coope
